title: feat(core,app-shell): execute the declarative row-level `operation: 'update'` action
body:
Fixes #7551

Executes the declarative row-level `operation: 'update'` action — the objectui half of objectstack#14092, consuming `@objectstack/spec` 17.3.0's `ActionSchema.operation` / `patch` (spec half: objectstack PR #15077).

Note on spelling: this body writes TypeScript generics with **square** brackets (`Record[RunnableActionType, …]`) instead of angle brackets, including inside the one verbatim quote below. GitHub's body sanitizer eats short angle-bracket-shaped fragments, so the transliteration is there to keep the quote readable rather than half-swallowed. The source says angle brackets.

## Step zero — the install probe, which is this card's release criterion

Comment `5555380342` pins the criterion by name: **installability, not upstream merge**, and forbids the other reading in as many words. The claiming seat could not take the probe (the shared checkout has no install — the control `zod` was empty too, so the zero was a broken instrument, not an absence). Taken here, in a worktree that installs, after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`.

Resolved from **`packages/core`**, which declares `@objectstack/spec` at `^17.3.0` (the repo root does not resolve it). Installed version **17.4.0**.

| leg | input | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **SUBJECT** | `{ name, label, operation: 'update', patch: { status: 'done' } }` | **ACCEPTED** |
| **CONTROL A** | `{ name, label, type: 'script', target: 'handlers/ping' }` | **ACCEPTED** — the schema works at all |
| **CONTROL B** | `{ …, operation: 'BOGUS_CONTROL' }` | **REFUSED** (`invalid_value` at `operation`) — the probe discriminates |

Parsed subject: `{"name":"mark_done","label":"Mark Done","type":"script","operation":"update","patch":{"status":"done"},"refreshAfter":false}`, and `ActionType.options` reads `["script","url","modal","flow","api","form"]` — **no new member**, exactly as the card relays.

Two corrections to the relay, both found by re-deriving rather than trusting it:

- **Control A's first spelling was wrong and the probe said so.** `{ type: 'script', script: … }` is REFUSED — `script` is not a key, and `execute` (the obvious second guess) is a spec-17 tombstone whose refusal prescribes the rename. The handler slot is `target`. A control that fails is not a control; the leg above is the corrected one.
- **A first sweep of the refusal clauses was contaminated** by a fixture whose `name` was too short, so every leg came back REFUSED for a reason that had nothing to do with the key under test. Re-derived with a valid name.

With that fixed, every clause the card relays reproduces against the **installed** schema: `target`, `body`, `method`, `bodyExtra`, `bodyShape`, `recordIdParam`, `recordIdField`, `onSuccess`, `opensInNewTab`, `newTabUrl` each REFUSED beside `operation: 'update'`; `list_toolbar` REFUSED in `locations` (a `custom` refinement) while `list_item` / `record_header` / `record_more` / `record_related` / `record_section` are accepted; `type: 'script'` accepted and every other explicit type refused; `patch` without `operation` refused; `operation` with neither `patch` nor `params` refused.

## Executor contract

**1. `operation` is read before `type`.** The dispatch in `ActionRunner.execute` now branches on `operation === 'update'` ahead of both the registered-handler lookup and the built-in table. The card's key argument is checkable and the file states it itself — verbatim from the comment above the `builtinExecutors` declaration:

> Built-in dispatch, one entry per runnable action type.
>
> A table rather than a `switch` because the type annotation is the guard: `Record[RunnableActionType, …]` stops compiling the moment `@objectstack/spec` adds an `ActionType` this runner has no executor for. That is the whole Tier-2 failure class for actions — a spec name that validates at save and then does nothing at run time (#2942) — converted into a build error.

Because `ActionType` did not move, that `Record` compiled unchanged across this bump — which is precisely why the key needs its own branch: by the time `type` is consulted, an update action is indistinguishable from any other script action.

**2. The write is performed by the platform action route.** The runner composes `{ recordId, params }` and hands it to the registered `script` dispatch, which POSTs `/api/v1/actions/{object}/{action}`. One re-location worth recording: the card says to POST "the same route `executeScript` already posts", but on this base **`executeScript` does not post anything** — it evaluates client-side, and names the route only in its refusal text, prescribing `createServerActionHandler`. That factory is what owns the POST, and app-shell registers it under `script` (`handlers: { api, flow, script: serverActionHandler, modal }`). Routing through it is what makes "the same route" true. A consumer with no such dispatch registered gets a loud refusal naming the remedy — never a client-side `dataSource.update()`, and never the silent fall-through to `executeActionSchema`.

**3. Forward sites — enumerated by the gate, not by hand: 4.** Making the runner read the two keys moved the gate's runtime-read set from 39 to 41 and each declared surface's owed count from 25 to 27, and it then named exactly four surfaces: `action:button`, `action:icon`, `action:group`, `action:menu`. All four now forward the pair. `element:button` is **not** among them and needed no entry — its contract is spec's `InlineActionSchema` pick list, so the gate derives an inline owed set that does not carry these keys. The spread-based hosts (`DeclaredActionsBar`, `RelatedRecordActionsBridge`, `ObjectGrid`, `page:header`'s `dispatchHeaderAction`) carry the keys through by construction; each was read rather than assumed. The two app-shell `bodyExtra` sites are deliberately unchanged: they are readers inside the `type: 'api'` handlers, and that path's client-side `dataSource.update` is exactly what clause 2 forbids for this key.

`patch` merges **under** the collected `params`, per the spec's own wording. With `undoable: true` the Undo affordance captures prior values of exactly the fields written — the collected params included, since restoring only part of an edit while reporting a full undo is worse than offering none.

The in-tree note recording the 2026-09-05 maintainer ruling on the 17.3.0 bump ("record both as justified omissions now; forward only the key a runtime actually reads, once its semantics are read from upstream — no speculative forwarding") is updated rather than left standing: its condition is now met, and it claimed in the present tense that no runner branch reads the keys and no surface forwards them.

## Verification

All figures below are from runs at the final head **`acee73257`**. Type-checks and vitest ran behind `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`.

| check | verdict |
|:--|:--|

| `vitest packages/core/src/actions/` | exit **0** — 25 files, **437** tests |
| `vitest packages/components/src/renderers/action/` | exit **0** — 19 files, **299** tests |
| `vitest` components `__tests__` + app-shell metadata-admin inspectors | exit **0** — 269 files, 2955 tests (one file failed on first run, fixed, see below) |
| `node scripts/check-action-forward-parity.mjs` (objectui#4050) | exit **0** — 5 surfaces, 41 runtime-read keys, 19 justified, 7 known gaps |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the final 11 files | exit **0** |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | exit **0** — 8038 tracked text files |
| `pnpm check:spec-floors` | exit **0** (see the prerequisite note below) |

Governed-queue guard verdict, verbatim:

```
✅ NOT GOVERNED — 11 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.
   An ordinary pull request: the normal review and merge-queue route applies.
```

`check:spec-floors` first exited 1 with four `no-artifact` findings — packages with no build output for it to judge. That is a **prerequisite failure, not a finding**: the gate says in its own words that it refuses to return "nothing to inspect, therefore clean". It is directly relevant here (this change makes `packages/components` and `packages/app-shell` read 17.3.0 keys while both declare `^17.0.0`), so the packages were built and it was re-run for a real reading: green, because it judges by exported symbol names and these two are property names, which move no floor.

### Ablation

Mutation: the `operation`-first branch deleted from `ActionRunner.execute`, through `ablation-replace.mjs` so the write is verified against the disk rather than against an exit code.

```
anchor   x1 -> x0
blob     946ab814ae3e1830a3e639c4f145aeae8b3dcce3 -> 5470faea208f1b5229851fb5306f930abbcccff6
ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0, blob 946ab814ae3e -> 5470faea208f
```

Predicted direction before running: **red**. Observed: **5 failed | 5 passed** of 10.

The inputs the two implementations disagree about are chosen so the disagreement is the defect, not a signature change. The sharpest is the request body: ablated, the action still reaches the route (its `type` is `script`), and the POST carries

```
  {
    "note": "typed by the user",
    "recordId": "rec_2",
-   "status": "done",
  }
```

— the route asked to write a record, handed no field values, answering success for having written nothing. The second is an action carrying **no `type` at all** (a `sys_metadata` row rehydrated unparsed): ablated, it lands in `executeScript` and reports `No script provided for script action`.

The 5 that stayed green are the reverse pins and the no-`undoable` case — a script action without `operation` is byte-for-byte unaffected. That asymmetry is the evidence the ablation was targeted rather than broad.

Restore proven on both legs:

```
blob after restore  946ab814ae3e1830a3e639c4f145aeae8b3dcce3
blob at HEAD        946ab814ae3e1830a3e639c4f145aeae8b3dcce3
git diff HEAD       empty
```

No ablation artefact remains and no permanent test file was added for it. The subject resolves through a **relative source import** (`../ActionRunner`), not through the package's `exports`, so no `dist` preflight applies — stated because the absence of one is otherwise indistinguishable from a forgotten one.

### One pin needed updating, and why that is not a weakened gate

`action-forward-precedence.test.tsx` enumerates the exact key set and order `action:button` / `action:icon` compose. It went red with `+ operation, + patch` and nothing else moved. The declared lists gain the two names in the position the forwards occupy (beside `bodyExtra` / `bodyShape`, which shape the same request). The reading the pin exists to give is unchanged: the list is compared whole, so an insertion that genuinely reordered its neighbours would still surface as several moved names rather than two added ones.

### Lint narrowing, declared

Narrowed to the 10 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files: **exit 0, 0 errors, 79 warnings** (all pre-existing `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` and `react-refresh/only-export-components`, which are warnings and do not fail).

- **Population** — read from `eslint.config.js` itself, not guessed: the selector is `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` and the `ignores` block removes `dist`, `.next`, `node_modules`, `public`, `.source` and three literal untracked build artefacts. Over tracked files that is **4986**.
- **Count** — **10**, read from the `--format json` output's own length, not from my file list.
- **Invariance** — type-aware linting is **not** enabled: the config extends `tseslint.configs.recommended` (not `recommendedTypeChecked`) and declares no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` anywhere, and no rule in `eslint-rules/` reads another file from disk. Each file's verdict is therefore a function of that file plus the shared config; this diff touches no config and no shared rule, so it cannot move the verdict of any of the 4976 untouched files.

One methodological correction: the first narrowed run used `--no-inline-config` and reported 5 errors. That flag was **mine, not this repo's** — the lint script here is a plain `eslint .` per package — and it manufactured those errors by disabling `eslint-disable` comments that legitimately exist in two of the renderers. The reading above is the one taken as the repo actually lints.

## Scope and delivery

Draft, deliberately, and left that way. objectui `AGENTS.md:330` tells a green non-governed PR author to self-merge; that clause conflicts with this dispatch, the conflict is filed as objectstack#19128, and until it is ruled this acts on the stricter side. No label is applied (this repo names no dev-applied label; `needs:contract-review` is the seat's). No ready flip, no auto-merge, no CI wait.

The claim comment carries no `Clause-②:` line to copy into this body — recorded rather than invented. `Check Changeset` reads this body and the changeset is present and green on its own gate.

## Acceptance notes

Observations made while working, filed nowhere and not fixed here:

- The card's executor contract cites `executeScript` as the thing that "already posts" the action route. It does not, on any base in this repo's recent history — the POST has lived in `createServerActionHandler` since objectui#2904. The card's line numbers are from `3e01cb55` and were re-located rather than trusted, as instructed.
- The spec's `undoable` description says "`patch` names exactly the fields whose prior values are captured", while an update action may also write collected `params`. This implementation captures the union (every field actually written), on the ground that a partial restore reported as a full undo is the worse failure. For a patch-only action — the shape the sentence describes — the two readings are identical. Worth a spec-side word if the narrower reading was meant.
